title: Migrating Between Version Control Systems
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and boundaries of migrating between version control systems.
Choose and interpret a Git command relevant to migrating between version control systems using a disposable repository.
Verify the result with repository state or history and identify one safety limitation.

content.intro: This lesson introduces migrating between version control systems as part of Recovery, Maintenance, and Migration. It follows the supplied Git curriculum and adds an original explanation, an inspectable command example, troubleshooting notes, and a practice task.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
**Core idea.** VCS migration needs a source-specific export/import approach and verification of authors, commit history, branches, tags and line endings. Git’s fast-import/export tools work with Git data streams and are not a universal converter for every VCS.

For **Migrating Between Version Control Systems**, keep the named subtopics in view: Repository export and import concepts; Preserving commit history; Mapping authors and branches; Verifying the migrated history. Treat those as the scope of this lesson, then practise the smallest workflow that demonstrates the idea.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: **Before you run a command:** decide what state you are inspecting or changing, identify whether the effect is local or remote, and write down what evidence would count as success. This exports Git data; it does not by itself import an arbitrary external VCS. For migrations, use source-system-specific export/import tools and verify authors, branches, tags and history.

content_blocks.run_instructions: This exports Git data; it does not by itself import an arbitrary external VCS. For migrations, use source-system-specific export/import tools and verify authors, branches, tags and history.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Use a disposable repository. If the exercise changes state, check git status and git log before and after; discard the practice directory only after confirming it contains no valuable work.
content_blocks.limitations: The CodeLeaf web lesson page does not execute arbitrary Git commands. Run commands locally in a disposable repository with a Git version appropriate to your task. Placeholder paths, branches, commit IDs and repository URLs must be replaced with values from that practice repository.

content_blocks.title: Safety and verification checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Start with git status --short --branch. For destructive or history-rewriting operations, review the exact target, create a recovery reference when appropriate, and keep valuable work backed up. Never put credentials, access tokens or private keys in course submissions.

task: In a disposable repository, create an annotated practice tag on a known commit, inspect the tag target, and compare the current work with the previous tag before writing a release note.
hints: Start by reviewing: Repository export and import concepts.
Use a read-only inspection command before any operation that changes files, refs or remote state.
After the example, verify with git status --short --branch and/or git log --oneline --graph as appropriate.
expected_output: A stream of Git commit/tree/blob and reference data for the current repository, when it has refs to export.

common_mistakes.problem: Running a state-changing command without confirming the target repository or branch.
common_mistakes.why: A command may affect the wrong working tree or move a reference that other work depends on.
common_mistakes.fix: Check git rev-parse --show-toplevel and git status --short --branch before proceeding.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a command succeeded because no error was visible.
common_mistakes.why: Some Git commands are silent on success, and some expected actions are blocked by repository state or permissions.
common_mistakes.fix: Verify status, log, references, remote state or the named output explicitly.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example placeholder literally or applying a destructive example to valuable work.
common_mistakes.why: Paths, branch names and object IDs depend on the current repository; restore/reset/clean operations can discard work.
common_mistakes.fix: Substitute real practice values, use a disposable repository, and preview changes before proceeding.

summary: Migrating Between Version Control Systems is covered through these syllabus topics: Repository export and import concepts; Preserving commit history; Mapping authors and branches; Verifying the migrated history.
Choose the command for the intended effect; understand whether it changes files, the index, local references, or remote state.
Verify the result, record unexpected output, and retain a recovery path for risky operations.
